evidence: Top-level package names (batch_processing, markdown_to_pdf, text_to_speech, format_conversion, html_website, canvas_integration, module_organization, file_validation, publish) map clearly to domain capabilities — a new engineer can read the directory and understand the system's surface
CLAUDE.md documents a 4-layer architecture (Layer 0-4) that is mostly honored in module-level imports
Each package consistently provides main.py (public API), utils.py (internals), config.py (constants), and __init__.py (re-exports) — this is a coherent internal pattern applied uniformly
canvas_integration/__init__.py exposes only 3 public functions, demonstrating appropriate surface restraint
html_website/__init__.py exposes only generate_module_website — single-function public surface is clean and predictable
batch_processing/__init__.py re-exports 18 symbols — the full internal API, eliminating encapsulation value of the __init__.py boundary

canvas_integration/main.py has sync_module_structure (line 123) that does nothing but call upload_module_to_canvas with a comment 'For now, we'll use the upload function' — a public API function that is semantically distinct but behaviorally identical, creating false ownership boundaries

scripts/ directory contains generate_all_outputs.py, generate_module_renderings.py, flatten_published.py which are thin wrappers — appropriate — but the publish pipeline also lives partly in the top-level publish.py (repo root), partly in scripts/publish_all.py, and partly in src/publish/ creating a fragmented entry-point map

log_style.py as a standalone file in batch_processing breaks the main/utils/config convention: it is neither main logic nor pure utils nor config, introducing a fourth file type in one package that does not exist elsewhere

format_conversion module exposes batch_convert and convert_file as its primary API, but batch_processing/main.py never calls format_conversion — it calls the sub-converters directly — making format_conversion's stated role as composition layer invisible in practice

strengths: Package names are strongly domain-aligned and self-explanatory
The main/utils/config/init internal structure is applied uniformly across all 15 packages
Public surfaces on leaf packages (html_website, canvas_integration) are appropriately small
The layer model is documented and directionally followed, making the intended architecture legible
Scripts are thin orchestrators that delegate to src/ rather than containing business logic
high_level_elegance.issue_character: The decomposition is structurally sound at the naming level but has several ownership blurs: format_conversion's role is undermined by batch_processing bypassing it, canvas_integration has a public stub that violates its own contract, and the publish/logging infrastructure has grown beyond its domain without being refactored into a clearer shape.
high_level_elegance.score_rationale: This codebase scores above average on high-level structure: the package taxonomy is genuinely domain-aligned, and the uniform internal pattern (main/utils/config) lowers cognitive load for new engineers. The score is held back by three significant ownership blurs — format_conversion is architecturally documented as a composition layer but is bypassed in the main pipeline, sync_module_structure is a dead-stub public API that misleads about canvas_integration's capabilities, and the four-way split of the publishing entry point (repo-root publish.py, scripts/publish_all.py, scripts/generate_all_outputs.py, src/publish/) creates navigational confusion. These are not cosmetic; they represent places where subsystem change boundaries would surprise a developer.

issues.summary: format_conversion is documented as a composition layer but bypassed entirely by the main pipeline, making its role invisible
evidence: batch_processing/main.py calls render_markdown_to_pdf directly from markdown_to_pdf, generate_speech from text_to_speech, and convert_file from format_conversion only for DOCX and HTML — not as the single conversion boundary
format_conversion/main.py provides convert_file and batch_convert as its public API, suggesting it should be the single conversion entry point
The architecture doc (CLAUDE.md) places format_conversion at Layer 2 as a composition layer, but the Layer 3 batch_processing module talks to Layer 1 modules directly
issues.suggestion: Commit to one of two options: (a) route all format conversions through format_conversion/main.py so it is the actual composition boundary, or (b) remove format_conversion as a distinct layer and merge its routing logic into batch_processing. Leaving both in place obscures ownership.

issues.summary: canvas_integration.sync_module_structure is a public API stub that delegates entirely to upload_module_to_canvas with no distinct behavior
evidence: Line 144-146: `# This is similar to upload_module_to_canvas but focuses on structure / # For now, we'll use the upload function / return upload_module_to_canvas(...)`
sync_module_structure is exported in __init__.py and __all__, making it part of the public contract
A developer calling sync_module_structure expecting sync semantics (idempotent, diff-based) will get full upload behavior instead
issues.suggestion: Either implement distinct sync semantics in sync_module_structure (checking existing canvas state and only uploading changed files) or remove it from the public API until it has real behavior. The current stub actively misleads about module capability.

issues.summary: log_style.py is a fourth file type in batch_processing that breaks the package's own main/utils/config structural convention
evidence: Every other package has exactly main.py, utils.py, config.py, __init__.py
batch_processing has an additional log_style.py containing emoji dicts and formatting helpers
log_style.py content (formatting constants + utility functions) maps squarely to either config.py (constants) or utils.py (helpers) — it is not a justified fourth type
issues.suggestion: Move FORMAT_EMOJI, STATUS_EMOJI, CONTENT_EMOJI, STEP_EMOJI constants to config.py and format_summary/format_module_result/section_header/step_header/validation_status functions to utils.py. Delete log_style.py to restore the uniform package structure.

issues.summary: batch_processing/__init__.py re-exports the full internal API (18 symbols), eliminating package encapsulation
evidence: __init__.py re-exports all 18 public and semi-public functions from main.py and utils.py
This means any caller of batch_processing can reach internal helpers like ensure_output_directory-equivalents through the package surface
By contrast, html_website exposes 1 symbol and canvas_integration exposes 3 — the inconsistency makes batch_processing's intended public contract ambiguous
issues.suggestion: Reduce __init__.py to the functions that form the genuine public API consumed by scripts/ (process_course_modules, process_course_labs, process_course_syllabus, clear_all_outputs, generate_dry_run_report, get_courses_to_process, get_formats_to_process). Remove low-level worker functions like process_module_to_pdf, process_module_to_audio, process_module_to_text from the re-export surface.

root_causes: format_conversion and batch_processing were developed without a firm decision about who owns the conversion boundary, leaving both in an ambiguous state
canvas_integration.sync_module_structure was stubbed in anticipation of future work and never completed or removed
log_style.py grew organically from formatting needs without enforcing the established file structure convention
likely_symptoms: HLE-04 is partly symptomatic of the missing public-API discipline also visible in CMA-01
